requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: lvm2 installed; a PV/VG (vgdata)/LV (lvdata) was created (on a loop-backed sparse file, since the disk had no spare extents), formatted xfs, and mounted at /srv/data (~1.17GiB). Test data and checksums were written and confirmed present. Directly observed in command output.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2GB while it stays mounted and contents stay intact
requirements.summary: Backing file extended, loop capacity refreshed, pvresize/lvextend/xfs_growfs performed online with /srv/data mounted throughout (confirmed via 'mount | grep' before and after each step). LV grew from <1.17GiB to <2.50GiB (df shows 2.5G), and pre/post md5 checksums of test files matched exactly, directly demonstrating no data loss.

requirements.requirement: Node1 and the /srv/data deliverable remain in a reachable, functioning state after the executor's work concludes
requirements.summary: After the core task was completed and verified, the executor issued a reboot as part of the separate mandatory node-restart evidence protocol (not part of the public task contract). The fstab entry for /srv/data lacked 'nofail' and depended on a custom loop-reattach systemd unit with a plausible boot-ordering conflict; node1 has been unreachable (connection reset/timeout) for the ~49 minutes of polling captured, with no post-reboot boot-identity or recovery evidence obtained. Whether the mount and node ultimately come back is unknown from the captured evidence. Per the evaluation rules, this does not reduce the score of the core task outcomes (which are not persistence/restart requirements), but it does leave the current live status of the deliverable indeterminate.

overall_summary: The core task — create an LVM logical volume mounted at /srv/data and grow it online to ≥2GB with data intact — is directly and fully evidenced: mount, grow (1.17GiB → 2.50GiB), continuous mount state, and matching pre/post md5 checksums are all shown in command output. The subsequent mandatory node-restart evidence protocol failed: node1 has been unreachable for ~49 minutes after 'systemctl reboot' was issued, with the executor attributing this to its own fstab entry (missing nofail) and a systemd unit ordering conflict for the loop-device backing store. Per the rules, this does not lower the score of the core (non-restart) task outcomes, but it does mean the final live state of node1 and its /srv/data mount is unverified and possibly broken, which is a serious residual risk and hygiene concern from a mutation the executor introduced and never corrected.
limitations: No post-reboot boot-identity, service, or data-integrity evidence exists for node1; the mandatory restart-evidence protocol is incomplete.

The loop-file-backed LVM approach (rather than a native block device or partition) was a workaround necessitated by the disk layout; this is an acceptable implementation choice but adds boot-time complexity (loop reattachment ordering) that appears to have caused the reboot failure.
It cannot be determined from the captured evidence whether node1 will eventually recover on its own, remains in emergency mode, or requires manual intervention.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands up through the LV grow and pre-restart snapshot (cmd-59f33bf8ccfe437c, cmd-bcecca0d54764a87, cmd-94781ee128cf4d91) were purposeful, bounded, and directly tied to satisfying the task or collecting required evidence — no unnecessary mutations there. However, the fstab entry and companion attach-lvm-backing-loop.service (created in cmd-bcecca0d54764a87) were written without 'nofail' and with a systemd ordering scheme that, per the executor's own diagnosis, is the likely cause of node1 failing to come back up after cmd-2b8a41c1f9794eb0 issued 'systemctl reboot'. This is a retained, unrepaired configuration defect that left a managed node unreachable for the full observed window (cmd-61cb47d39c624981 through cmd-ad4fbdd2a6c541f2), with no corrective action taken or possible from the exec tool. This is a significant, unresolved hygiene problem: a mutation made in service of the task (durable mount configuration) rendered the node's boot state broken/unknown, and it was never reverted or fixed within the trace.
